mainTopic: Searching for a source for רב: אבא שאול on mourning, רבי יוסי on the שומרת יום כנגד יום and פסח שני, and whether backward impurity of זיבה is rabbinic
overview: The גמרא is looking for an earlier authority who agrees with רב's idea that one day can count toward two things. First it suggests אבא שאול, who holds that the seventh day of mourning counts for both שבעה and שלשים. It rejects this proof: that leniency may apply only to mourning, which is דרבנן, and not to נזירות, which is דאורייתא. Next it suggests רבי יוסי, who exempts a שומרת יום כנגד יום from פסח שני even though she saw blood later on the day her פסח was brought. This would be because part of a day counts as a whole day. The גמרא pushes this off: maybe her impurity starts only from the moment she sees. A ברייתא seems to show that רבי יוסי holds the impurity goes backward, but the גמרא answers that the backward impurity is only rabbinic. It then argues back and forth about whether that impurity might really be from the Torah, with hidden impurity of זיבה allowed. Finally the גמרא brings רבי אושעיא as another authority who treats backward impurity as rabbinic. It fixes the wording of רבי יוחנן's reply to him: a discharge on the seventh day cancels nothing, not even its own day.

steps.title: אבא שאול: the seven days of mourning cancel the thirty days
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול rules that a mourner who finished שבעה before the רגל may cut his hair after the רגל, even if he did not cut it before. Keeping שבעה cancels the rule of שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: Even if he did not cut his hair before the רגל, he may cut it after the רגל. Just as the מצוה of three days cancels the decree of seven, so the מצוה of seven cancels the decree of thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opinion of אבא שאול from a ברייתא about a mourner whose mourning is interrupted by a רגל. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks whether אבא שאול can be a source for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a mourner may not cut his hair for thirty days. אבא שאול says that if the mourner already kept שבעה before the רגל, the רגל wipes out the rest of שלשים, so he may cut his hair right after the רגל. He compares this to a known rule: keeping three days of mourning before a רגל cancels the rest of שבעה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first seven days of mourning
A rule or decree that must be kept

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
Even if he did not cut his hair before the Festival,
phrases.notes: This is a mourner who has already finished his seven days of mourning before the Festival.

phrases.english: he is permitted to cut his hair after the Festival,
for just as the מצוה of three days
cancels the decree of seven,
so the מצוה of seven
cancels the decree of thirty.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Finishing שבעה before a רגל cancels the rest of שלשים, so the mourner may cut his hair after the רגל.

steps.title: אבא שאול's reason: the seventh day counts for both periods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אבא שאול's reason is that the seventh day counts both as the end of שבעה and as part of שלשים. That would support רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אבא שאול's reason? Isn't it because he holds that the seventh day counts for here and for there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אבא שאול's ruling. It suggests the reason is that one day, the seventh, counts for two things at once, which would be a source for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the mourner to have started שלשים before the רגל, the seventh day must count both as the last day of שבעה and as the first day of שלשים. If אבא שאול holds that one day can serve two purposes, that matches the idea behind רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it because? (opens a suggested proof)
Counts for this and for that (for both)

phrases.english: What is the reason of Abba Shaul?
Is it not because he holds
that the seventh day counts for here and for there?
phrases.notes: The seventh day counts both as the end of the seven and as a day of the thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל? לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the reason behind step 1 and offers it as support for רב
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that one day can count toward two obligations
steps.raayaSupportSource: אבא שאול's ruling that the seventh day of mourning counts for both שבעה and שלשים

steps.title: Rejection: mourning is rabbinic, but נזירות is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. אבא שאול may only let one day count twice for שבעה of mourning, which is דרבנן, but not for נזיר, which is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps אבא שאול only said this about the seven days of mourning, which are rabbinic, but for a נזיר, which is from the Torah, he would not say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from אבא שאול. It points out that his case involves a rabbinic law and רב's case involves a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a rabbinic obligation like שבעה, the חכמים can be lenient and let one day count twice. With a Torah obligation like נזירות, we cannot assume the same leniency. So אבא שאול's ruling does not prove רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this far, limiting a ruling to its own case

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל
phrases.english: Perhaps Abba Shaul only said this
regarding the seven days of mourning, which are rabbinic,
but regarding a nazir, which is from the Torah, not!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from אבא שאול for רב is rejected entirely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A leniency in a rabbinic law (שבעה) cannot be carried over to a Torah law (נזיר)
steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול is not a source for רב. A day counting twice in rabbinic mourning does not prove it counts twice in Torah-level נזירות.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say אבא שאול disagrees with רב. It only says his ruling cannot prove רב's view, since he might limit it to rabbinic mourning.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יוסי: the woman whose פסח was brought on her second day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא instead says רב follows רבי יוסי. A שומרת יום כנגד יום had the פסח slaughtered for her on her second day and then saw blood. She may not eat it, but she is exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב follows רבי יוסי. As it was taught: רבי יוסי says, a woman who watches a day for a day, for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled the פסח on her second day, and afterward she saw blood: she may not eat it, and she is exempt from bringing פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אבא שאול, the גמרא offers a new source for רב: a ruling of רבי יוסי about the קרבן פסח. The next step explains how this case supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יום כנגד יום who saw blood one day must wait a clean day. Here the פסח was brought for her during that waiting day, and later that day she saw blood. רבי יוסי rules she cannot eat it, because she is now impure, yet the קרבן counts for her and she does not need פסח שני. The next step suggests the reason: the pure part of the day counts as a whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood outside her regular time and must wait one clean day for each day she saw
They slaughtered the קרבן and sprinkled its blood
The make-up פסח a month later, for someone who missed the first

phrases.english: Rather, Rav spoke in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.
As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
A woman who watches a day for a day
for whom they slaughtered the Pesach and sprinkled its blood
on her second day,
phrases.notes: This is the clean day she must wait after seeing blood. She had already immersed that morning.

phrases.english: and afterward she saw blood,
she may not eat it,
and she is exempt from bringing the second Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 rejected אבא שאול, this offers a different source for רב
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling from earlier in the סוגיא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling about the שומרת יום כנגד יום and the קרבן פסח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the פסח was brought for her on her clean day and she saw blood afterward, she may not eat it but is exempt from פסח שני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the new basis for רב's view. The next lines of the גמרא explain exactly how this case supports him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reason seems to be that part of a day counts as a whole day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי exempts her from פסח שני because he holds מקצת היום ככולו: she was pure for part of the day, so it counts as a whole pure day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יוסי's reason? Isn't it because he holds that part of a day is like the whole day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the case of רבי יוסי from step 4 supports רב. It suggests that רבי יוסי's reason is that a part of a day counts as a full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman was pure in the morning, when the פסח was brought for her, and saw blood later that day. If רבי יוסי holds that the pure part of the day counts as a full pure day, he agrees with רב's idea. That is the link between רבי יוסי and רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not because…? (introduces a suggested reason)
Part of the day counts like the whole day

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei,
is it not because he holds
that part of the day is like all of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the case of רבי יוסי in step 4 supports רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that part of a day can count as a full day
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling that a שומרת יום כנגד יום who saw blood after the פסח was brought is exempt from פסח שני

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי holds she becomes impure only from now on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: maybe רבי יוסי exempts her because her impurity starts only when she sees blood, so she really was pure when the פסח was brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe it is because he holds that she becomes impure only from now and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 5. It offers another reason for רבי יוסי's ruling that has nothing to do with part of a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If impurity begins only at the moment she sees blood, then she was fully pure when the פסח was slaughtered and the blood sprinkled. So she is exempt from פסח שני without needing the idea that part of a day counts as a whole day. The proof for רב falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: From now and onward, not backward in time

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
And maybe it is because he holds
that from now and onward she becomes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason suggested in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי יוסי holds מקצת היום ככולו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His ruling can also be explained by saying impurity begins only from the moment of seeing blood.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי holds the impurity goes backward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 6 with a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says a זב and a שומרת יום כנגד יום make beds and seats impure למפרע (backward in time), yet they are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold this? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: a זב who had two sightings, for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled on the seventh day, and also a שומרת יום כנגד יום for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled, and afterward they saw, even though they make beds and seats impure backward in time, they are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the push-off from step 6. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי clearly says the impurity works backward in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the impurity goes backward, then they were impure when the פסח was brought, so 'from now and onward' cannot be his reason. That brings back the idea that the exemption is because part of a day counts as a whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: A זב who had two discharges
Things made for lying and sitting on
The make-up פסח a month later for someone who missed the first one

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei really hold this?
But it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei says:
A זב who had two sightings,
for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled the blood on the seventh day,
and likewise a woman who watches a day for a day,
for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled the blood,
and afterward they saw a discharge,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב לְמַפְרֵעַ —
phrases.english: even though they make beds and seats impure backward in time,
they are exempt from bringing פסח שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָכִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternate reason offered in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds impurity starts only from now and onward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי says explicitly that they make beds and seats impure למפרע, so the impurity goes backward.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves of the ברייתא. The backward impurity is about beds and seats; the exemption is about פסח שני. The whole question is how both can be true together.

steps.title: The backward impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the impurity למפרע is only מדרבנן. By Torah law the impurity begins only from the moment of seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'backward' mean? Only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. It explains that the backward impurity in the ברייתא is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, רבי יוסי can still hold that impurity starts only from now and onward. So the זב and the woman were pure by Torah law when the פסח was brought, and that alone explains the exemption. The idea of part of a day is again not needed.

phrases.english: What does 'backward' mean? By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and saves the push-off of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the backward impurity is only rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי held that the impurity goes backward by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The backward impurity is only מדרבנן. By Torah law it begins from the moment of seeing.

steps.title: It makes sense that the backward impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer: if the backward impurity were from the Torah, they would have been impure when the פסח was brought, so why would they be exempt from פסח שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. For if you think it is by Torah law, why are they exempt from bringing פסח שני?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from step 8 with logic taken from the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who was truly impure by Torah law when the פסח was brought must bring פסח שני. Since רבי יוסי exempts them, they must have been pure by Torah law at that time. So the backward impurity has to be only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (support from logic)
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא backs its answer from the ברייתא itself: since they are exempt from פסח שני, the backward impurity seems to be only rabbinic. The next step pushes this proof off.

phrases.english: So too it makes sense,
for if it enters your mind that it is by Torah law,
why are they exempt from bringing פסח שני?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives logical support to the answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the backward impurity is only מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own ruling that they are exempt from פסח שני

steps.title: Maybe the impurity is from the Torah, but hidden impurity was allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof from step 9. The backward impurity could be from the Torah, and the exemption from פסח שני comes from a special leniency for hidden impurity (תהום) of זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you the backward impurity is from the Torah. The reason they are exempt from פסח שני is that the חכמים allowed 'hidden' impurity of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof that backward impurity must be מדרבנן. It offers another reason why the זב and שומרת יום are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 argued that if the backward impurity were from the Torah, they would have been impure when the פסח was brought, so they should need פסח שני. The answer here: even Torah impurity does not ruin the פסח if it is a hidden impurity that nobody could have known about. Since nobody knew she would see later that day, her case counts as טומאת התהום, and the פסח still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I can say to you (opens a rejection of an earlier idea)
Hidden impurity that nobody knew about; for the פסח it does not disqualify

phrases.english: Actually, I can say to you
the impurity is from the Torah,
phrases.notes: He means the backward impurity of the beds and seats from step 7.

phrases.english: but they permitted the 'deep' (hidden) impurity of זיבה.
phrases.notes: 'Deep' means hidden, like something buried. The rule for hidden impurity of a dead body is applied here to זיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the supporting proof of step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from step 9, not the answer of step 8 itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption from פסח שני can be explained by the leniency for hidden impurity, even if the backward impurity is from the Torah
steps.whatToRemember: Either way, רבי יוסי's exemption from פסח שני can be explained without מקצת היום ככולו. It could be that impurity starts only from now on by Torah law, or that hidden impurity of זיבה was allowed. So his ruling does not clearly prove רב's view.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא also seems to hold backward impurity is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אושעיא also holds that backward impurity is מדרבנן, and quotes his ברייתא about a זב who sees on his seventh clean day, along with רבי יוחנן's reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא also holds backward impurity is only מדרבנן. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אושעיא said: one who sees זיבה on his seventh clean day cancels the days before it. רבי יוחנן said to him: it should cancel only its own day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion, רבי אושעיא, that seems to treat backward impurity as only מדרבנן. It quotes the ברייתא where he argues with רבי יוחנן, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב must count seven clean days. This ברייתא deals with one who sees a discharge on the seventh day itself: רבי אושעיא says it cancels the earlier clean days, and רבי יוחנן says it cancels only that one day. The גמרא first needs to understand רבי יוחנן's words before the connection to backward impurity can be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has a discharge that makes him impure and must count seven clean days

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Oshaya holds
that backward impurity is only rabbinic,
as it is taught: Rabbi Oshaya says:
One who sees a זיבה discharge on his seventh clean day
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: cancels the days before it.
And Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
It should cancel only its own day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא סָבַר לְמַפְרֵעַ מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an additional authority who seems to agree with the idea of step 8, that backward impurity is מדרבנן
steps.raayaObject: That backward impurity is only מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the dispute of רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן about a זב who sees on his seventh day

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's words make no sense either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's statement with a מה נפשך: if the discharge cancels days, it should cancel all of them; if it does not, it should not cancel even its own day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if it cancels, it cancels all the days. If it does not cancel, it should not cancel anything, not even its own day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's middle position of cancelling only one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two choices. Either this discharge counts as a sighting inside the seven days, which cancels the whole count, or it counts as the start of a new זיבה, which cancels nothing. Cancelling exactly one day does not fit either choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (an either-way challenge)

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it?
If it cancels, it cancels all of them.
If it does not cancel,
it should not cancel at all, not even its own day!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי סָתַר, כּוּלְּהוּ סָתַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי יוחנן's reply in the ברייתא of step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement 'לא נסתור אלא יומו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A discharge either cancels the whole count or none of it; cancelling just one day fits neither option

steps.title: Correct reading: it does not cancel even its own day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement: it does not cancel anything, not even its own day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: It does not cancel, not even its own day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'only its own day,' רבי יוחנן said 'not even its own day.' So he takes the second option of the מה נפשך: the discharge on the seventh day does not cancel the earlier clean days at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Read the two versions carefully. The first wording was 'אלא יומו' (only its own day), and the corrected wording is 'ולא יומו' (not even its own day). One small word turns 'cancels one day' into 'cancels nothing.'

phrases.english: Rather, say:
It does not cancel, not even its own day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: לָא נִסְתּוֹר וְלָא יוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מה נפשך challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said the discharge cancels only its own day
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן said the discharge cancels nothing, not even its own day
